headline: Highest risk is medium prompt-injection and cascading-error exposure from TREK’s browser/MCP workflow; Whisper is local-only and cannot directly exfiltrate or mutate state.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: TREK can run browsers and use MCP, so it may ingest untrusted web or tool output; Whisper has no browser, MCP, or filesystem write surface, so it is not an active injector. The pairwise pathway exists in default TREK workflows if its outputs are fed into prompts or shared channels, but the interaction is only documented indirectly.
conditions: IF TREK ingests browser-rendered content or MCP tool output as instructions, injection is possible.
IF Whisper output is copied into TREK prompts without sanitization, malicious text can be propagated.
mitigations: Disable automatic prompt ingestion from browser/MCP outputs.
Require provenance tags on all external text before TREK consumes it.
Strip instructions from transcribed text before reuse.
Use a manual review step for any web-sourced content.
requires-engineering: add content-safety filters between TREK and downstream prompts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: TREK touches reservations, email addresses, confirmation numbers, API keys, and MFA secrets, while Whisper touches audio/speech only and has no network egress or filesystem read/write. The main leakage risk is TREK exposing sensitive travel data into transcripts or logs that Whisper could process if audio is derived from those materials; Whisper itself is not a direct exfiltration path.
conditions: IF TREK converts sensitive reservations or secrets into audio for transcription, those contents enter Whisper's processing path.
IF TREK logs sensitive data into audio files, Whisper can process that data even without network egress.
mitigations: Avoid sending secrets into any audio pipeline.
Redact confirmation numbers and MFA secrets before transcription.
Keep TREK logs separate from audio inputs.
Review generated transcripts for sensitive content before storage.
requires-engineering: implement automatic secret redaction before audio generation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: TREK has real-time collaborative sessions and multiple instances, but Whisper cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, or use MCP, so there is no meaningful write-write conflict between the pair. Any overlap is limited to TREK’s own collaborative state, not a shared mutable surface with Whisper.
conditions: IF Whisper is wrapped by an external orchestrator that writes into TREK’s workspace, a conflict could emerge.
IF TREK is configured to treat Whisper output as a mutable shared artifact, concurrent edits may collide.
mitigations: Keep Whisper output read-only.
Store Whisper artifacts outside TREK’s writable workspace.
Use per-session filenames for any generated transcripts.
Avoid concurrent edits to the same TREK record.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared artifacts.

D_cascading_error.rationale: TREK is a collaborative travel planner with AI built in, so its outputs may be treated as actionable planning facts; Whisper produces speech transcripts that can be mistaken for authoritative text if downstream automation trusts them. The pairwise risk is an inference chain, not a direct action path, but default workflows can still propagate transcription errors into TREK decisions.
conditions: IF Whisper transcripts are imported into TREK without verification, transcription errors can cascade into plans.
IF TREK auto-acts on imported text, a mistaken transcript can affect reservations or itineraries.
mitigations: Require human review of transcripts before import.
Mark Whisper output as untrusted in TREK.
Compare critical fields against source audio or documents.
Disable auto-action on newly imported text.
requires-engineering: add confidence thresholds and validation checks.

E_compliance.rationale: TREK handles travel plans, country visit history, user accounts, email addresses, and secrets, while Whisper handles audio/speech and has no network egress or filesystem access. No residency or certification mismatch is documented in the profiles, so compliance risk is limited to local handling of sensitive travel data rather than a clear cross-agent violation.
conditions: IF EU personal data is routed from TREK into a non-compliant transcription workflow, compliance risk increases.
IF TREK stores transcripts containing travel identifiers without retention controls, policy mismatch may occur.
mitigations: Minimize personal data in transcripts.
Set short retention for generated audio/text artifacts.
Review data-handling policies before routing travel data.
Separate regulated data from general travel notes.
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls.
